newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela bolivar ends firm despite TEM yield drop.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela bolivar ends firm despite TEM yield drop.

text.p: The Venezuelan bolivar firmed in moderate trade to end at 480.75/481.75 per dollar despite a fall in TEMs, used as a benchmark for wider interest rates, and only modest Central Bank dollar sales, traders said.
On Tuesday the unit closed at 481.25/482.25 per dollar.
"There were a lot of dollars being sold on the interbank market ... it must have been due to high foreign demand for TEMs," said one trader at a large bank.
Yields on key six month Central Bank bills bucked market expectations when they fell 123 basis points to 17.48 percent in Wednesday's regular auction.
"We had been expecting TEM yields to rise, but their drop didn't push up dollar demand at all," said another trader.

Venezuela's foreign exchange market is unusual in that the Central Bank is its largest single supplier of dollars, which blurs the difference between the Central Bank supplying liquidity and intervening.
